extracted.subtask_description: Core craft principles and practical habits for producing literary prose, drawn from Annie Dillard's The Writing Life. Focuses on process, attitude, and concrete daily practices that shape long-form creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spend It All
rubrics_metrics.description: "Spend it all, shoot it, play it, lose it, all, right away, every time. Do not hoard what seems good for a later place in the book, or for another book; give it, give it all, give it now."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't save your best material — use it now and trust more will come. Avoid hoarding promising lines or scenes for a supposed later use; commit generous material to the work at hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Following the Line
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing is "following a line of words."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat writing as a moment-to-moment activity: each word leads to the next. Let the 'line'—its internal logic and momentum—pull you forward; probe forward with the sentence-level flow rather than imposing a distant plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Years, Not Months
rubrics_metrics.description: A book takes 2–10 years. "Less is so rare as to be statistically insignificant."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect long timelines; do not judge a project's worth by how quickly it is produced. Fast writing rarely yields work that endures—allow extended time for depth and discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity over Generality
rubrics_metrics.description: "Don't tell the reader that someone was happy or sad. When you do that, the reader has nothing to see. She throws his clothes out the window. Be specific."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show concrete detail instead of labeling emotions or states. Use particulars—actions, images, sensory detail—to let the reader infer feeling and meaning rather than summarizing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Your Unique Perspective is the Project
rubrics_metrics.description: "You are the only one of you. Your unique perspective, at this time, in our age, whether it's on Tunis or the trees outside your window, is what matters."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center the distinctness of your viewpoint as the primary asset of your work. Trust that your individual observation and voice are the central contribution, regardless of topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Writing Life is Brutal but Necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The dedication, absurdity, and daring of writing as a vocation; not for everyone, but those who can do it owe it to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept writing as a demanding, sacrificial practice. Recognize the emotional and existential difficulty as part of the vocation and a requirement for producing serious work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cutting is Half the Job
rubrics_metrics.description: "You write it all, discovering it at the end of the line of words. The line of words is a fiber optic, flexible as wire; it illumines the path just before its fragile tip. You probe with it, delicate as a worm."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize revision and cutting as essential to the creative process. Discover material in the act of writing, then ruthlessly pare and refine; the exploratory 'line' reveals what must be kept and what must be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools / Daily Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical habits and tools listed: Walk; Read deeply in your own field; Write daily; Make peace with the fact that the room will be lonely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt daily, sustaining practices: regular walking to feed attention, continual deep reading within your field, consistent daily writing, and acceptance of solitude as part of the work environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline as Faith
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer keeps showing up not because they know it will work but because the act of writing is its own form of devotion to the work emerging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View discipline as an act of faith—regular attendance to the page is both the method and the belief that work will emerge. Persist without guaranteed results; consistency itself is generative.
